notes: Cool nights give fruit that is nearly always high in acidity, with abundant fruit flavor.
New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc has asparagus, gooseberry and green flavors, with grassy, citrus and passion fruit notes.
Most New Zealand wine is made to drink young.
Hawke's Bay led New Zealand's Cabernet Sauvignon, though early wines were green and vegetal.
Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc is what New Zealand is best known for, with green, gooseberry, citrus and passion fruit notes.
Chardonnay here leans to citrus, peach and melon.
Its Pinot Noir often has darker fruit and more savory character than Marlborough's.
Gisborne Chardonnay leans toward citrus, peach and melon.
Pinot Noir is perfumed and balanced, with ripe red berries, cherry and plum, spice and light herbal notes.
Sauvignon Blanc is rich in tropical fruit and herbaceous notes, usually without too much pungency, with a crisp, balanced palate.
Wines from the clay-rich Moutere Hills tend to be more robust, with texture, weight and denser tannin.
The stony Waimea Plains favor aromatic whites with clear varietal character, and reds with fine tannin.
